title: Contextual KV compression — sprint scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick running notes from sprint pairing with Priya and Mika (late Feb -> early Mar 2026). Goal: explore cheap, online compression of KV caches to reduce memory and network transfer for long-context serving while preserving next-token quality for span-local continuation.

Summary takeaways:
- Hybrid parametric + sparse compression seems promising: small linear projection (32->8b) + per-token residual hashing to recover frequent patterns. Good latency tradeoffs vs full float16/8 quantization for sequence lengths > 64k.
- Key failure mode: over-compressing attention key vectors from early context loses persona tokens that matter for long-range coreference (observed in convo rerank A/B).
- Cache-chunking: chunk KV by recency windows (16k tokens), maintain high-fidelity hot-chunks and aggressively compress cold-chunks. This reduces peak GPU memory by ~30% in rough sim.
- Network cost: streaming compressed chunks between boxes (Dedicated -> Private hybrid routing) can drop egress by ~40% if compression ratio > 3x and CPU decompress cost is <1ms/token. Need benchmarking.

Quick notes on papers / prototypes to revisit:
- arXiv:2602.01234 "Sparse Residual KV Compression" — interesting simple residual tables; re-run with our model tokenizer and LoRA weights.
- Transformer-engineering thread: empirical note about attention head sensitivity to low-rank approximations. Add to eval checklist.
- Prototype repo (local): redwood-inference/kv-compress-proto — small C++/CUDA kernel that packs 8-bit runs; incomplete readme.

Experiments to run (ordered):
1) Reproduce toy sim: GPT-like 1.2B, synthetic dialog, baseline float16 cache vs 8-bit linear quantizer + residual hash. Metric: next-token perplexity at 1k/4k/16k windows; measure CPU/GPU time to compress/decompress. (Owner: me, due 2026-03-12)
2) Chunking ablation: keep window sizes [4k, 8k, 16k, 32k], hot-chunk threshold tuned on recency+salience score (salience heuristic: last mention frequency * recency weight). Measure memory saving and quality drop. (Owner: Priya)
3) Integration: implement streaming compressed-chunk transfer in local Dedicated dev infra. Hook into request router to allow fallback to full-fidelity if quality regression detected. (Owner: Mika + SRE buddy)

Evaluation checklist (what we actually measure):
- Delta next-token PPL at multiple distances (0-64, 64-512, 512-16k)
- End-to-end tail latency impact (p95/p99) including compress/decompress and network transfer
- Cost per request delta (GPU mem footprint -> concurrency -> cost)
- Failure surface: cases where compressed context flips generated facts or pronoun referents (collect examples)
- Interaction with quantization (8-bit weights) — compounded degradation?

Open questions / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: a tiny learned projection (32->16->8b) trained with reconstruction loss on in-domain contexts will preserve salient tokens better than uniform scalar quantization.
- Hypothesis B: hashed residuals help recover recurring phrases (e.g., named entities) but introduce noise for rare tokens — need tunable per-token budget.
- Can we combine semantic-similarity clustering on KV keys to store representative prototypes instead of exact keys for cold-chunks? Tradeoff: semantic loss vs compression gains.

Implementation notes / commands:
- local bench script: tools/kvbench/run_local.sh --model gpt-1b --seq-lens 4096,16384 --compressor linear8-resid --workers 4
- quick patch (WIP): patch in repo at feature/kv-compress-streaming. See TODO in README for decompression fast path.

Collected examples (manually curated) — cases where compressed cache caused visible issues:
- convo-id 20260219-045: pronoun resolution failed after compressing early persona lines ("Alex is an engineer...") -> model attributed job to wrong name.
- eval scenario: legal doc summarization where compressed cold-chunk lost citations -> hallucinated reference numbers.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Run toy sim and post results in #ml-kv-compress by 2026-03-12. Attach perf numbers + a handful of counterexamples.
- Design small loss function variant (reconstruction + entity-preservation weight). Start training run on 8 A100 hours (cost estimate: 6 credits).
- Prep a one-pager for Solutions Eng: explain tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Private when shipping compressed caches across regions.

Notes to self (thinking aloud):
- Might be worth splitting compression into two pathways: semantics-first (dense prototypes for meaning) and tokens-first (exact local tokens for factual anchoring). Runtime picks per-chunk based on salience classifier.
- Think about auditability: decompressed chunks must be reconstructable for compliance audits (in Private deployments). Consider storing deterministic seeds for hashing + lossy index maps to allow reproducibility.

References / links to read later:
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.01234 (reservation: cite when we have numbers)
- https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-compress-proto (internal prototype)
- https://discuss.transformer.news/thread/9284 (engineering thread)

End of scratchpad. Will clean up after first experiment run.
